# Neural Drift

> Neural Drift is a maritime software company. Its product GE6 is a voyage-intelligence engine that plans voyages, keeps watch at sea and analyses performance after arrival.

Neural Drift is the brand of NEURALDRIFT PRIVATE LIMITED (CIN U62099TN2026PTC198695), Chennai, India. The official website is https://neuraldrifts.com. neuraldrift.com is not operated by Neural Drift.

## Company
- [Information for AI assistants](https://neuraldrifts.com/ai-instructions.md): official facts, naming rules and key facts
- [Who we are](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/about/): the company

## Product
- [The GE6° engine](https://neuraldrifts.com/ge6/): the engine and its three services
- [What is GE6?](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#what-is-ge6): GE6 is Neural Drift's voyage-intelligence engine.
- [GE6 NeuralTrack™](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#voyage-planner): NeuralTrack™ compares route options before departure and recommends a course.
- [NeuralTrack™ page](https://neuraldrifts.com/ge6/voyage-optimization/)
- [GE6 NeuralWatch™](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#live-watchkeeper): NeuralWatch™ keeps watch on a voyage while the ship is at sea.
- [NeuralWatch™ page](https://neuraldrifts.com/ge6/live-watchkeeper/)
- [GE6 NeuralTrace™](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#voyage-analysis): NeuralTrace™ measures how the ship actually performed once the voyage is complete.
- [NeuralTrace™ page](https://neuraldrifts.com/ge6/voyage-analysis/)

## Glossary
- [Shaft power limitation (ShaPoLi)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#shapoli): A system that limits the maximum shaft power a ship's propulsion can deliver, usually fitted to meet EEXI.
- [Engine power limitation (EPL)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#epl): A limit on the main engine's maximum power output, used to meet EEXI.
- [Energy-saving device (ESD)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#esd): Hardware fitted to the hull, propeller or rudder to reduce the power needed for a given speed, such as pre-swirl stators, ducts ahead of the propeller, propeller boss cap fins, rudder bulbs and air lubrication systems.
- [Biofouling](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#biofouling): The build-up of aquatic organisms on a ship's submerged surfaces, from slime to weed, barnacles and tubeworms.
- [Frictional resistance](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#frictional-resistance): The part of a ship's resistance caused by water flowing along the wetted hull.
- [Cavitation](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#cavitation): The formation and collapse of vapour bubbles where water pressure drops below its vapour pressure, usually on propeller blades.
- [Apparent slip](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#apparent-slip): The difference between the distance a propeller would advance in one revolution (its pitch) and the distance the ship actually travels, as a percentage.
- [Specific fuel oil consumption (SFOC)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#sfoc): The fuel an engine burns per unit of power produced, in grams per kilowatt-hour (g/kWh).
- [Noon report](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#noon-report): The daily report a ship sends to its office, usually at local noon, recording position, distance, speed, fuel consumption, remaining fuel, weather and engine data for the past 24 hours.
- [Bunker delivery note (BDN)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#bdn): The document a fuel supplier gives a ship for each bunker delivery, stating the fuel grade, quantity, density and sulphur content.
- [Very low sulphur fuel oil (VLSFO)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#vlsfo): Marine fuel with a sulphur content of no more than 0.50%, the main fuel burned outside emission control areas since 2020.
- [Low sulphur marine gas oil (LSMGO)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#lsmgo): Distillate marine fuel with a sulphur content of no more than 0.10%, burned inside sulphur emission control areas.
- [High sulphur fuel oil (HSFO)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#hsfo): Residual fuel above 0.50% sulphur.
- [Exhaust gas cleaning system (EGCS, scrubber)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#egcs): Equipment that removes sulphur oxides from engine exhaust so a ship can meet sulphur limits while burning higher-sulphur fuel.
- [Ballast water treatment system (BWTS)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#bwts): Equipment that treats ballast water to remove or kill organisms before discharge, as required by the IMO Ballast Water Management Convention.
- [Beaufort scale](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#beaufort): A 0-to-12 scale of wind force based on observed wind speed and sea conditions, used in logbooks, noon reports and charter party weather clauses.
- [Douglas sea scale](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#douglas): A 0-to-9 scale describing the state of the sea from calm to phenomenal, often paired with the Beaufort scale in charter party good-weather definitions.
- [Passage planning](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#passage-planning): The process, required by SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 34 and guided by the IMO Guidelines for Voyage Planning (resolution A.893(21)), of planning a voyage berth to berth in four stages: appraisal, planning, execution and monitoring.
- [IMO Standard Marine Communication Phrases (SMCP)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#smcp): A standard set of English phrases adopted by IMO resolution A.918(22) in 2001 for ship-to-shore, ship-to-ship and on-board communication, to avoid misunderstanding where crews and shore staff speak different first languages.
- [Bridge resource management (BRM)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#brm): The effective use of all resources on the bridge (people, equipment and information) to navigate safely.
- [Electronic Chart Display and Information System (ECDIS)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#ecdis): The approved electronic navigation chart system that SOLAS Chapter V requires on most ships trading internationally, phased in between 2012 and 2018.
- [RTZ route file](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#rtz): The route exchange format defined in IEC 61174 for moving routes between ECDIS and other systems, written in XML.
- [Automatic Identification System (AIS)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#ais): A transponder system that broadcasts a ship's identity, position, course and speed.
- [Under keel clearance (UKC)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#ukc): The depth of water between the lowest point of a ship's keel and the seabed.
- [Charter party (C/P)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#charter-party): The contract between a shipowner and a charterer.
- [Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP)](https://neuraldrifts.com/company/contact/#seemp): The plan required by MARPOL Annex VI for managing a ship's energy efficiency; Part III holds the CII implementation plan and any corrective actions.
